question.text: Under Section 11(4) of the SEBI Act, which of the following measures can SEBI take pending investigation or inquiry?

answer.text: All of: suspending trading of any security on a recognised stock exchange; restraining persons from accessing the securities market; impounding and retaining proceeds or securities of a transaction under investigation
Suspend trading of any security in a recognised stock exchange
Restrain persons from accessing the securities market
Impound and retain proceeds or securities of a transaction under investigation

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 11(4) empowers SEBI to take each of these interim measures: suspend trading, restrain market access, suspend office-bearers, impound proceeds/securities, attach bank accounts (up to 90 days), and direct non-disposal of assets. The Trap: Each listed measure is a valid interim power, but the question asks about every measure SEBI can take. Cross-Exam Context: SEBI's interim powers are tested in NISM Series III-A and III-B. Distributor's Pro-Tip: SEBI's interim powers are very broad and can be exercised even before completing investigation - maintain compliance at all times.
